label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, A, C where the asset was C, A, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The wheel's outline matches the brief's words: a round rim with six spokes from a hub, 32 across. A rusted post on a flat base is added behind and below it (front, left, back, right and below views). The brief asks for a wheel alone, and the post sticks out of the wheel's outline in the left, right and back views and in the below view.

M2.reason: Measured 32 across against the 32 the brief gives (sizeOff 0.001). Height 33 and depth 13 come with the post, so they are not checked against the brief.

M3.reason: The parts a valve wheel needs are all there: a rim (a ring of about 14 sides, grey steel), six red spokes running from rim to hub, and a red hub at the centre. Small rim joints show as silver nubs at the right and back-left edges of the rim. The rusted post is not a part the brief names, so it is charged under M1, not here.

M4.reason: The brief's red paint is on the spokes and hub, and the rim is bare grey steel, which is what worn-to-steel means here. Colours are the same hues across views, with no stray colour on any region.

M5.reason: The wear the brief asks for is there: the rim reads as bare steel with a sheen, and the spokes stay red and meet it at the rim. Rust mottling on the post and speckle on the spokes sit at a sharpness close to the other textures.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test: over four readings, each in its own order, judges never picked the asset as the one not made by Valve (picked D, D, A, C where the asset was at C, A, B, D).

M7.reason: The wheel's face is the front, upright, with spokes and hub facing the viewer. The post's flat base sits on the origin and the object stands on it.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. At 392 triangles it is under the 422 that Half-Life's most-spending prop of this size uses, and under twice the median of 99. The rim, spokes and column all read closed in the views, and the base plate's underside is a closed disc in the below view. Nothing visible is open, inside out or floating.
